sentence: This project makes nanobiologics that block trained immunity and probes for nuclear imaging, and helps handle radioactive materials safely.
This project studies how changes in human DNA between people and between cells in the body affect how the body works, its traits and evolution.
This project studies how the structures at the ends of human chromosomes help protect genomes in cancer cells, stem cells and cells undergoing meiosis.
This project studies specialized progenitor cells in the walls of lung blood vessels and how they are controlled in vascular disease.
This project builds machine learning methods that find variations in the human genome that cause Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies how differences among the mitochondria inside cancer cells affect how melanoma develops and how it is treated.
This project studies how cells repair broken chromosomes and how repair links to the response to DNA damage, mostly in budding yeast.
This project tries to find out how Tropomyosin 1 limits the making of blood stem cells from cultured induced pluripotent stem cells.
This project builds methods that explain how clinical AI models reach their answers, and applies them to skin disease.
This project studies how cells copy chromosomes past obstacles such as DNA damage and nucleosomes without losing genetic information.
This project tries to find out why gene edited human cells block HIV-1 better in some cases than in others.
This project studies how an enzyme called acetyl-CoA synthetase 2 helps T cells work inside tumors where nutrients are scarce.
This project uses machine learning to combine many kinds of molecular data and find what drives age-related cognitive decline.
This project delivers mRNA in lipid nanoparticles to lung air sacs to treat leaky capillaries and harmful white blood cells in acute respiratory distress syndrome.
This project builds AI tools that find and predict immune-related adverse events in cancer patients given immune checkpoint inhibitors.
This project studies why immune T cells fail to eliminate cancer cells and tests ways to reprogram them to kill cancer cells.
This project studies the epigenetic mechanisms that keep the Meibomian gland healthy and that change in aging.
This project supports pilot projects and technologies for cancer research, including tumor immunology, cancer imaging and cancer metabolism.
This project studies what a protein called FK506-binding protein 5 does in the heart and how its loss in cardiomyocytes and fibroblasts promotes atrial fibrillation.
This project tries to find out why HIV-1 infection is uncommon in people with systemic lupus erythematosus, looking at interferon signalling and iron.
